name.ja: アメデオ・アヴォガドロ

overview.en: Amedeo Avogadro was an Italian scientist known for his contribution to molecular theory, including what is now known as Avogadro's law and Avogadro's number.

early_life.en: Avogadro was born in Turin, Italy. He initially studied law and practiced as a lawyer before turning to science, becoming professor of mathematical physics at the University of Turin.

impact.en: Avogadro's hypothesis that equal volumes of gases contain equal numbers of molecules provided a key bridge between atomic theory and measurable quantities, unifying chemistry and physics.

event.en: Became professor at University of Turin

title.en: Essay on Determining the Relative Masses of Elementary Molecules

description.en: Paper proposing that equal volumes of gases contain equal numbers of molecules

text.en: Equal volumes of all gases, at the same temperature and pressure, contain the same number of molecules.
